overview: This Senate resolution let the Senate confirm a large group of the President's nominees at once, instead of debating and voting on each one separately. It made it in order to consider 108 nominations from the Senate's Executive Calendar together, "en bloc," in a single action. The nominees included officials at the Departments of State, Labor, Commerce, Justice, Education, Veterans Affairs and others, a member of the Securities and Exchange Commission, and ambassadors to more than a dozen countries. The Senate adopted the resolution on October 3, 2025, by a vote of 51 to 46.
for: Supporters say considering many nominees together clears a long backlog of open government positions that would otherwise take weeks of floor time to fill one by one.
against: Critics say confirming over a hundred nominees in a single action reduces the chance for the Senate to scrutinize and debate individual nominees for important posts.
